builder_plan.scenario: Start with one repeated product task that has a measurable failure or cost.
builder_plan.change: Read the methods and identify one change you can isolate in that workflow.
builder_plan.baseline: Your current implementation on the same held-out tasks.
steps: Locate the paper's implementation and check its license, model support, data needs, and hardware requirements. Stop here if you cannot obtain the required artifacts.
Save a small set of representative product tasks and expected outcomes. Keep evaluation tasks out of any training or tuning, and choose quality and cost limits before running.
Run the baseline and the proposed change on identical inputs. Keep other settings fixed and repeat paired runs to expose variation.
Save per-task outputs, failures, timings, and all usage costs. Review regressions before expanding the test.
builder_plan.measure: Successful outcomes, response time, human rework, and total cost per successful task.
builder_plan.decision: Keep the change only if it meets your preselected quality and latency limits and improves the metric you care about after setup and operating costs. Otherwise retain the baseline. This is an exploration plan, not a validated recommendation.

title: Skeletal Prototypes on Iterative Nerve Expansions
summary: SPINE replaces point-set prototype reduction with per-class embedded 1-complexes built from class-conditional Mapper graphs, where edges and vertices both enter the nearest-complex decision rule. Cost is construction overhead comparable to discriminative prototype methods, with a vertex-fitting phase under a classification objective; no GPU or large infrastructure is required. It can fail when prototype budgets are very small or very large (gains concentrate at moderate budgets), and results are validated only on seventeen small benchmark datasets, so transfer to high-dimensional embeddings or production-scale data is unproven.
rationale: The method is relevant only if the reader maintains classical nearest-prototype classifiers on small tabular-style datasets, a niche outside typical constrained-GPU LLM production work, so monitoring rather than adoption is warranted.
technique: Graph-based skeletal prototypes for prototype reduction

claims.statement: SPINE replaces point-set prototype reduction with per-class embedded 1-complexes built from class-conditional Mapper graphs, where edges and vertices both enter the nearest-complex decision rule. Cost is construction overhead comparable to discriminative prototype methods, with a vertex-fitting phase under a classification objective; no GPU or large infrastructure is required. It can fail when prototype budgets are very small or very large (gains concentrate at moderate budgets), and results are validated only on seventeen small benchmark datasets, so transfer to high-dimensional embeddings or production-scale data is unproven.

Highest mean accuracy and best average rank across seventeen benchmarks versus seven prototype-reduction methods at matched budget; significantly better than five of seven under Wilcoxon signed-rank tests with Holm correction; faster than generalized LVQ on fourteen of seventeen datasets.
